title: When to Do Newborn Photos: The 5–14 Day Window in the RGV
description: Wondering when to do newborn photos? See why days 5–14 work best, when to book, and how RGV families plan for early or late arrivals and older babies.
h1: When to do newborn photos: the sleepy first two weeks
dek: The short answer is 5 to 14 days after birth. Here’s why that window works so well, when to reserve your spot, and what to do if your baby is already a little older.
intro:
The best time to do newborn photos is between 5 and 14 days after birth, when most babies sleep deeply and still curl up the way they did before they were born. To be sure of a spot in that window, book during your second or third trimester — the exact date is set once your baby arrives.

Below, we walk through when to do newborn photos for families across the Rio Grande Valley. You’ll find why those first two weeks work so well, how booking and scheduling happen, what changes if baby comes early or late, and your options if your little one is already a bit older.

sections.h2: Why days 5–14 are the sweet spot
sections.html:
In the first two weeks, most newborns spend long stretches in a deep, heavy sleep. They’re also still used to being snug and tucked in, so they settle easily into the soft, curled-up poses people picture when they think of newborn portraits — knees tucked, tiny hands near the face, wrapped in a soft knit.

That sleepiness is what keeps the session calm. Moving from a wrap on a little bed to a basket takes only small, gentle adjustments, and a sleepy baby usually stays settled through them. Adrisabel is trained in safe newborn posing and has photographed hundreds of babies, so each change is made slowly and with care.

Starting around day 5 leaves the first few days for rest, recovery and getting home. After about two weeks, many babies are awake for longer and like to stretch out, and they’re often less content in tightly curled poses. That’s a normal, lovely change — it simply means a different kind of session suits them better.

sections.h2: When to book: your second or third trimester
sections.html:
So when should you do newborn photos if baby isn’t here yet? Reach out during your second or third trimester, and we’ll save a spot around your due date. Booking early takes one more decision off your plate before those tired first days at home.

This is also when you choose your session. Sunshine is all about baby, with 8 edited photos, 2 outfits and 2 backdrops. Wonderland brings in siblings and parents, with 15 edited photos, 2 outfits and 4 backdrops. You can compare both on our newborn photography page.

If you’re planning maternity portraits too, booking maternity is the perfect time to reserve your newborn session as well. Our guide on when to take maternity photos covers the bump side of the timeline.

sections.h2: How the date is set when baby arrives
sections.html:
When your little one is born, just send us a message — a call or text to (409) 354-3075 works, or a note through the booking form. We reply within 24 hours and set your session for a day within the 5–14 day window. There’s no need to do the math yourself; just tell us the birth date, and we’ll count the days.

Early or late babies are completely normal. Your due date is a guide, not a deadline, so the session is set when baby actually arrives. Whether your little one comes two weeks early or a week late, the plan stays the same: send a message, and we’ll find a day inside the window.

Expecting twins?

Twins can be added to any package and include 4 extra photos. They often arrive a little ahead of schedule, and that’s fine too — let us know when they’re here, and their session is set within the same 5–14 day window.

sections.h2: Choosing the best day within the window
sections.html:
There’s no single right day between day 5 and day 14, so deciding when to take newborn photos within that window comes down to your family’s week. Some parents like to come in closer to day 5, while everything still feels brand new; others prefer a few more days at home to rest and settle into feeding first.

Both work well. A few quick questions can help you choose:

  • Is your partner free on certain days? Sessions run Monday through Saturday by appointment (we’re closed Sundays), so a Saturday may be easier if work is a factor.
  • Are big brothers or sisters joining? For a Wonderland session, pick a time of day when they’re usually rested and happy.
  • What else is on the calendar? Those first two weeks often include checkups for baby and for mom, so choose a day with nothing else scheduled.
  • How are you feeling? Recovery looks different for everyone, so take the extra days if you need them.

sections.h2: Already past the newborn window? Here are your options
sections.html:
Maybe the first weeks flew by, or you’re only now starting to think about photos. That’s okay. The 5–14 day window is ideal for sleepy, curled-up portraits, but it isn’t the only time to photograph your baby.

  • Almost two weeks old: send a Sunshine newborn session request right away, so we can look for a day before the window closes.
  • A few weeks old: Wonderland is for newborns and babies with the whole family, so it’s a lovely choice when you want baby, siblings and parents together in the photos. To follow the whole first year instead, Pixie Dust includes 5 milestone sessions, starting at 1 or 2 months.
  • Two months and up: Fairytale is our baby session for 2–11 months, made for first smiles, giggles and sitting up.

The photos change in a good way, too. Instead of tightly curled, sleepy poses, you get wide-open eyes, little expressions and, before long, those first smiles.

Babies don’t smile on command, so sessions for older little ones are built around baby’s mood, with play breaks, snacks and silly songs. You can read about each stage on our baby milestone photography page.

sections.h2: Planning the drive from across the Valley
sections.html:
Families come to the studio in the McAllen area from all over the RGV, so it’s worth thinking about the drive when you pick your day. From McAllen and Pharr, it’s just minutes. Mission is about 10–20 minutes away and Edinburg about 15–20 minutes, while Harlingen is about 40–45 minutes, Rio Grande City about 45–50 minutes and Brownsville about 60–70 minutes.

A newborn session takes about 2–3 hours, so with a longer drive on each end, it can fill a good part of the day. Keep the rest of that day light, and if a partner or grandparent can drive, mom can rest on the way there and back. The exact session location is shared after booking.

faq.q: Is one month too late for newborn photos?
faq.a: It’s past the sleepy 5–14 day window, but it’s not too late for beautiful photos. At that age, Wonderland captures baby with the whole family, and Fairytale welcomes babies from 2 to 11 months.

faq.q: Can I book a newborn session before I know my baby’s birth date?
faq.a: Yes — that’s exactly how newborn sessions are planned. We save a spot around your due date, a 50% deposit via Zelle reserves it, and the exact day is set once baby arrives.

faq.q: What if I’m not sure which session fits my baby’s age?
faq.a: Tell us your baby’s age or due date through our booking request form, and we’ll help you choose the right session.
